title: Hardcoded PIN in client-side code exposes authentication mechanism
reasoning: The PIN '0312' is hardcoded in the client-side React component. Anyone with access to the client bundle (which is always public in a web app) can read the PIN by inspecting the source. This defeats the purpose of the PIN as an access control mechanism. Authentication should always be verified server-side, and secrets should never be embedded in client code.
reproduction: Open browser DevTools, search the bundled JavaScript for 'PIN' or '0312', and the PIN is immediately revealed.
recommendation: Move authentication to the server. The PIN should be verified via an API call to a backend endpoint that checks the PIN and issues a session token or JWT. Never store secrets in client-side code.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist. Security testing would require code review or penetration testing to identify hardcoded secrets.
suggestedRegressionTest: Security review: ensure no secrets are present in client bundles. Functional test: verify PIN validation occurs server-side and client cannot bypass.
minimumFixScope: src/src/pages/MarkPortal.tsx - remove hardcoded PIN and implement server-side authentication
